@graph.description: This is a study on how two glycogen deficient Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 mutant lines (glgC-1 and glgC-6) respond to constant illumination compared to the wildtype. Cells were pre-cultivated in shake flasks under constant light. For the main experiment, one culture of each strain was grown in a multi-cultivator. After an acclimation to the conditions in the multi-cultivator (standard conditions) of 24 hours of light, the experiment was started. After 11 hours of light, the samples were taken. The files in this project contain the identifier EoD to signify this illumination period of 11 hours during the experiment. This experiment was repeated 4 times for a total of 4 replicates per strain.
@graph.name: Cultivation of glycogen deficient Synechocystis strains in constant light conditions

@graph.description: Two glycogen-deficient glgC knockout strains (∆glgC-1, ∆glgC-6) along with wt were cultivated in a multicultivator. The cultivation was begun with an entrainment phase of 24 h of light followed by 12 h of dark. Then the experiment started. Samples were taken after 11 h of illumination and experiment start. These samples are called end of day (EoD) samples. After one additional hour, the illumination was turned off and the dark period began. After 11 h of darkness the end of night (EoN) samples were taken. Sampling included enough volume for OD measurement, RNAseq, and metabolomics.
@graph.name: Cultivation of glycogen deficient Synechocystis strains in diurnal conditions

@graph.description: This work contains the characterisation of glycogen-deficient Synechocystis strains. Microfluidics were performed and images captured. In a multi-cultivator, a cultivation during a diurnal period of 24 hours was performed. For each strain, including wildtype, two samples were taken at the end of day and end of night timepoints. On these samples RNAseq and metabolomics were performed.
@graph.name: Glycogen deficiency impairs diurnal energy metabolism and cell division in Synechocystis
